provenance.Annotator model/name: Copilot SDK AI assistant (subagent; model version not exposed)
provenance.Collection method: AI-assisted cause annotation via Copilot SDK in VS Code; not human annotation.
provenance.Inter-annotator agreement: Not measured; single annotator, no adjudication.
provenance.Evidence shown: cases.json only: dev query text and metadata, source title/abstract, D50 top-20 titles (abstracts for the top 10), positive-grade papers outside the D50 top 20 (abstracts for grade 2), completed top-20 grades with label provenance and judge reasons, stage ranks and graded-loss attribution.
Cautions: Causes are an AI assistant's reading of titles and abstracts, not validated ground truth.
Grades are LLM judgments (GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-6 ASTRA reference, GPT-6 Terra completion), not human labels.
No relevance labels, rankings or other evidence were created or changed.

codebook.status: codebook-v0 was written before any case evidence was read. codebook-v1 was refined after reading cases.json for all 16 cases and before assigning any annotation; changes are listed below and the v0 causes were not removed.

changes.reason: Six of the ten lowest-nDCG cases have the source at D50 rank 1 as the only grade-2 paper; their loss comes from ordering partial matches, which no v0 code describes without calling it a system error.

changes.change: vocabulary_gap may apply to other relevant papers, not only the source.
changes.reason: In lowest-nDCG cases with the source found, paraphrased wording can still pull off-target papers into ranks 2-10.

changes.change: label_gap split into a primary rule (wrong grade 2 or clearly wrong grade 0) and a secondary-only rule (0-vs-1 inconsistency).
changes.reason: Partial-credit disagreements are common in the pool and would otherwise make label_gap the primary cause of every single-target case.

changes.change: Added the selection-reason rule and a primary-cause precedence order.
changes.reason: Several codes can fit one case; a fixed order makes the single annotator's choices reproducible from the rules.

rules: Assign exactly one primary cause: the most specific explanation supported by the shown titles and abstracts.
Use secondary causes only for additional explanations that are also supported by the evidence.
Stage (where the paper was lost) is computed by code, not annotated; mechanism causes are used only when no content-level cause is evident.
The primary cause must explain why the case was selected: for a source miss, why the source is outside the D50 top 10; for a lowest-nDCG case, where the graded loss comes from.

When several causes meet their decision rules, choose the primary in this order: query_generation_artifact, label_gap, competing_near_duplicate, acronym_or_rare_term, vocabulary_gap, single_target_partial_credit, broad_or_underspecified_query, rerank_demotion, stage1_miss.

causes.definition: The query describes the source's contribution in different words from its title and abstract (paraphrase or terminology mismatch).
causes.decision_rule: The source or other relevant papers satisfy the query, but their key concepts appear under different terms, and higher-ranked papers share the query's surface words rather than the specific contribution asked for.

causes.definition: The query hinges on an acronym, named method, dataset or rare term that retrieval or reranking fails to match or resolve.
causes.decision_rule: Removing or expanding one specific rare token would plausibly change the outcome, and that token is in the source but rare or ambiguous in the corpus.

causes.definition: Many papers fit the query about as well as the source; the source is not uniquely best, so the miss is more a measurement limit than a system error.
causes.decision_rule: Several top-10 papers satisfy every stated requirement of the query, and the query omits the details that distinguish the source.

causes.definition: A top-ranked paper addresses nearly the same specific problem and method as the source, displacing it.
causes.decision_rule: At least one top-10 paper matches the source's specific problem and approach, not just its general topic.

causes.definition: The generated query does not describe the source well: it emphasizes details absent from, peripheral to or inconsistent with the source abstract.
causes.decision_rule: A reader of the source title and abstract alone would not judge the source a strong answer to the query.

causes.definition: Relevance labels understate or distort quality: relevant-looking top-10 papers are graded 0 or are unjudged, or grades are inconsistent with the abstracts.
causes.decision_rule: As primary: a grade 2 on a paper that shares only a word or a different sense of a query term, or a grade 0 on a top-10 paper that satisfies all of the query's main constraints, and these grades account for much of the loss. Inconsistent 0-vs-1 grades among partial matches are recorded only as a secondary label_gap.

causes.definition: The query has one clear target (the source), which D50 ranks first or second; few or no other papers meet all its constraints, so the loss comes from how partial matches (grade 0 vs 1) are ordered below it, a metric and label-pool effect more than a user-visible failure.
causes.decision_rule: Source at D50 rank 1 or 2 with grade 2, no grade-2 paper outside the D50 top 10, and the papers below the source each meet only part of the query.

causes.definition: Residual mechanism code: the source or most missing relevant papers never reached the Decision 36 top 50, and no content-level cause is evident.
causes.decision_rule: Use only when the computed stage is Stage 1 and none of the content-level causes above is supported.

causes.definition: Residual mechanism code: the reranker had the source or better-graded papers in its pool but ranked less relevant papers above them.
causes.decision_rule: Use only when the loss is within the reranked pool, the displaced papers are clearly more relevant, and no content-level cause is evident.

annotations.rationale: The Welsh-media source (bias in Nation.Cymru's political reporting) is at rank 1 and is the only grade-2 paper, so the loss comes from ranks 2-10: non-Welsh political-bias papers graded 0 or 1 inconsistently (LLM political-bias detection at rank 2 and German ideology prediction at rank 3 get 0, while algorithmic partisanship and target-stance extraction get 1).

The topic-only query 'multimodal llm decoding strategies' fits many papers (seven top-10 papers are grade-2 multimodal decoding methods, mostly for diffusion MLLMs), so the greedy-decoding-for-VQA source is one good answer among many; Decision 46 placed it at 21, below grade-1 text-only dLLM decoding papers and the grade-0 Modality Collapse paper, so the refinement never re-scored it.

The BL19 source (inclusive evaluation frameworks for historical IR) is at rank 1 and is the only grade-2 paper; ranks 2-10 are generic IR benchmarks and cultural-heritage retrieval systems graded mostly 0, with inconsistent splits such as NeuCLIRBench graded 0 at rank 9 but NeuCLIRTech graded 1 at rank 10.

The keyword query hinges on 'slate', yet three of its four grade-2 papers have no slate component (Learning What Evaluators Value at rank 9, Pedagogically Aligned LLM Tutors at 38, the unranked LLM-evaluator narcissism paper), which inflates the ideal; separately, Decision 46 moved the source from Decision 36 rank 1 to 4 and the rank-one pin kept the grade-0 'Once Generated, Ranked' slate paper above it.

The source (sentence-level clinical provenance categorization) is at rank 1, but grade 2 also goes to papers that share only the word 'provenance' in another sense (PhysioTRACE provenance-aware stress tests at rank 7, DeconDTN provenance shift at 58, concept provenance in LLM query simulation at 81), which inflates the ideal and produces most of the Stage 1 loss.

Bekkers' equivariant-neural-fields paper is at rank 1 and is the only grade-2 paper; ranks 2-10 are other equivariant operators or neural-field papers graded inconsistently (EqGINO and groupoid-equivariant networks 0, PACE-FNO and Clifford Sheaf Neural Networks 1).

The Brazilian legal segmentation source is at rank 1 and is the only grade-2 paper; ranks 2-10 are Brazilian or other legal-retrieval papers without the segmentation contribution, graded inconsistently (NormasTCU and Domain-Adaptive Dense Retrieval for Brazilian Legal Search 0, JUA and PRecG 1).

The Lorentz neural network source is at rank 1 and is the only grade-2 paper in a corpus with few hyperbolic papers; the remaining loss is partial matches (Lorentz-equivariant jet taggers, hyperbolic retrieval for RAG) that Decision 46 left at 22 and 24 behind grade-0 generic neural-network theory papers, so the refinement never re-scored them.

The policy-QA RAG source (rank 1) and TimelyRAG (rank 2) are the only grade-2 papers; ranks 3-10 are generic or legal RAG QA systems split inconsistently between 0 (legal RAG, Doctor-RAG, HybridRAG) and 1 (PluriHopRAG, Matryoshka hierarchical RAG).

The source is at rank 2 behind a grade-2 recommendation-unlearning paper, but the paraphrase 'systemic prejudices' in 'generative suggestion engines' also pulled generic LLM-debiasing papers graded 0 into ranks 4 and 6-8, while recommender-specific erasure or debiasing papers graded 1 (TRACER at 76, CRAB unranked) sit outside the Stage 1 top 50; grades are also inconsistent (Fairness Pruning 0 vs the similar Fairness Evaluation and Inference Level Mitigation 2).

Seven grade-2 top-10 papers (e.g. DREAM, Grevo, Differentiable Semantic ID, Drift-Aware Continual Tokenization) address the same problem of item identifiers that evolve with collaborative signals during generative-recommender training, and the query's 'item IDs'/'generative search' wording differs from the source's 'item tokenizer'/'generative recommendation', so PIT stayed outside the Decision 36 top 100 (semantic rank 91, lexical outside 100).

The query restates RAG corpus-poisoning defense ('fake info', 'external search results', 'removing a page' for leave-one-out decoding) in web-search words, so both Stage 1 components rank RAGuard outside their top 100 and the top 10 fills with AI-search credibility and generative-engine-optimization papers (no grade-2 paper anywhere in the pool).

The query's 'low precision numbers', 'distributed private devices' and 'comprehensive look' stand for quantization, federated learning and survey, so Stage 1 ranked the federated-quantization survey 58th (semantic 32, lexical outside 100) while the top 10 are centralized FP4/NVFP4 low-precision training papers graded mostly 1.

DTCRS (recursive summarization trees), SVD-RAG (tree-organized RAG) and LLM-guided Hierarchical Search implement the query's 'hierarchy of summaries' retrieval as directly as the source, whose own terms ('abstract bridge tree', query entities) differ from the query, so Bridge-RAG was outside both Stage 1 components' top 100.

'Actively gather information' fits preference elicitation, clarifying questions, cold-start querying and agentic tool use alike, so many papers partly fit and only one pool paper is graded 2 (Ask to Be Sure, rank 2); the agentic tool-use source RecThinker never reached the Decision 36 top 100 (semantic rank 88), and the rank-one pin kept the grade-0 semantic-augmentation paper first.

RuleWorld (the benchmark in 'Beyond Factual Knowledge', rank 3) and 'LLMs Learn Better In-Context from Rules than from Examples' (rank 1) measure learning externally provided rules from context as directly as the CL-bench source, and the general question fits many in-context-learning papers, so CL-bench was outside both Stage 1 components' top 100.

candidate_fixes.proposal: Report source MRR@10 and success@1 beside nDCG@10 for single-target (known-item) queries, and report their below-source partial-credit loss as its own bucket rather than as a ranking failure.

candidate_fixes.evidence: Six of 16 cases; all have the source at rank 1, and in five it is the only grade-2 paper in the judged pool (the sixth has one more, at rank 2); known-item source MRR@10 is already 1.000.

candidate_fixes.proposal: Rewrite or expand every query into the corpus's technical terms (for example an LLM terminology rewrite or a hypothetical-abstract embedding) before Stage 1, fused with the original query.
candidate_fixes.status: proposal only: needs new LLM and embedding calls (paid), so not testable offline on saved data
candidate_fixes.evidence: Three primary and two secondary cases; in the two vocabulary-gap source misses the source is outside the lexical top 100 and either outside the semantic top 100 or at semantic rank 32.

candidate_fixes.proposal: Treat this as a measurement limit: report 'source or any grade-2 paper in the top 10' beside source R@10, and keep diverse near-duplicates rather than tuning toward the generating paper.
candidate_fixes.evidence: Three source misses where several grade-2 top-10 papers address the source's specific problem.

candidate_fixes.proposal: For future query sets, have the query generator add a distinguishing constraint for broad queries, and read broad-query source MRR as a measurement limit; frozen queries stay unchanged.
candidate_fixes.evidence: Two cases; broad-specificity source MRR@10 is lower than specific queries' while nDCG@10 is higher (segment table).

candidate_fixes.proposal: Tighten the rubric so grade 2 requires the query's sense of each key term (not a shared word), calibrate 0 versus 1 for partial matches, and audit the top-20 pool with a second judge in a new versioned label layer.
candidate_fixes.status: proposal only: needs new paid judgments and owner approval; no labels changed here
